context.transcript_excerpt: Welcome to the Namibia Oil & Gas Podcast, your weekly gateway to the latest news and developments shaping Namibia's dynamic oil and gas sector. It's Friday, 4th September, 2026, and I'm Harrison Musimoko with the latest news, updates, and insights from the Namibia oil and gas industry. Let's dive in. This week's top headlines. Gulp completes strategic partnership with Total Energies. ED procurement expands focus as Namibia's procurement landscape grows. Recon Africa's financing sets stage for next phase of Kavango West 1X. F&B and RMB Namibia launch beyond the barrel. Namibia's oil and gas industry is growing, and local businesses need to be ready for the opportunities ahead. The Namibia Local Content Conference and Exhibition 2026 will take place from 19th to 23rd October. 2026 in Windhook under the theme offshore technology as a pathway to securing Namibia's local content development. The conference brings together industry leaders, technology innovators, businesses and local content stakeholders to explore how offshore technology can drive local participation build capacity and create opportunities for Namibian businesses If you want to understand where Namibia energy sector is heading connect with key industry players and position your business for the future. This is the platform to be part of. Register now at www.nlcc.com.na slash registration dash form. Be in the room. Be part of the opportunity. be part of Namibia's energy future. GALP has completed a strategic partnership with Sotel Energies in Namibia, reshaping its portfolio and expanding its presence in one of the three offshore blocks. The company retains a 40% interest in PEL83, which includes the Mopane Discovery, while acquiring a 10% interest in PEL56 and a 9.39% interest in PEL91. The new portfolio gives GALP exposure to assets in different stages of development, including Venus, one of Namibia's most advanced development projects, and one that is progressing towards a final investment decision. The next key milestones include the new MAPANE exploration and appraisal campaign expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, alongside further progress on Venus towards FID. ED Procurement Consulting Services has expanded its offering to support Namibian businesses navigating the country growing procurement and investment opportunities Led by Veronica Munongena the company brings experience across public procurement mining telecommunications, and upstream oil and gas, with services covering procurement advisory, bid support, training, supplier development, and oil and gas procurement readiness. Founded in 2026, EDI Procurement has already been active in Namibia's public procurement space, particularly in bidder capacity and organizational development. Its latest focus is on helping SMEs and local suppliers strengthen compliance, governance, financial and operational systems, and technical capabilities so they are better prepared to compete for opportunities emerging across sectors such as oil and gas. Recon Africa has secured approximately C$15 million through a bought deal public offering to advance technical work at the Kavango 1X well in northern Namibia. The company plans to use the financing primarily for an open-hole horizontal sidetrack and production testing program focused on the Hutenberg Formation, with the Elanswood Formation remaining a secondary target. The planned horizontal sidetrack will provide great exposure to the target reservoir and generate additional information about its production characteristics Recon Africa expects the financing to close around September 10 subject to regulatory approvals while the results of the testing will be important in determining the reservoir's characteristics and potential commercial significance.
